Sample observations from category representations, templates, or cognitive models

Source: R/S7-generics.R, R/S7-stanfit-methods.R
sample_observations.Rd

Generates simulated cue observations by sampling from an individual category representation, a multi-category template, or a complete cognitive model.

  • For single representations (MVBU_CategoryRepresentation), samples \(n\) observations from the representation's distribution.

  • For templates (MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate), samples \(n\) total observations distributed uniformly across categories.

  • For cognitive models (MVBU_CognitiveModel), samples \(n\) total observations distributed across categories proportionally to the model's category_prior.

Usage

sample_observations(
  x,
  n = 1L,
  with_replacement = TRUE,
  randomize_order = TRUE,
  ...
)

## S7 method for class <MVBU_Stanfit>
sample_observations(
  x,
  n = 1L,
  with_replacement = TRUE,
  randomize_order = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An MVBU_CategoryRepresentation, MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate, or MVBU_CognitiveModel object.

n

Non-negative integer specifying the total number of observations to sample. Defaults to 1L.

with_replacement

Logical; for exemplar representations, specifies whether to sample exemplars with replacement (TRUE, default) or without replacement (FALSE). Ignored for parametric families.

randomize_order

Logical; whether to randomize the row order of the returned observations. Defaults to TRUE.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods (e.g., Ns or randomize.order for backwards compatibility).

Value

A tibble with \(n\) rows containing a category factor column (with levels matching category labels) and one numeric column per cue.

See also

plot_categories, likelihood, posterior

Examples

mod <- example_mvg_ideal_observer(n_cues = 2)
sample_observations(mod, n = 5)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   category   VOT f0_semitones
#>   <fct>    <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 /t/      95.0        -0.694
#> 2 /g/       5.54        1.68 
#> 3 /p/      62.5        -3.42 
#> 4 /p/      82.4        -5.93 
#> 5 /t/      64.9        -4.47
